transcript:
Meeting: SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture review - Sterling Insurance
Recorded: 2026-02-18 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood CSM) — Mark Reynolds (CISO, Sterling), Aisha Khan (Security Engineer), Liam O'Connor (IT Ops), Hannah Yu (Legal)

Summary: Quick posture review where Redwood walked through SOC 2 / ISO evidence, trust center access, controls mapping, and technical details around encryption/KMS, RBAC/SSO, audit logs, and data residency. Customer asked about private deployment options and least-privilege access to logs. Action items and next steps captured.

Topics: SOC 2 Type II report availability, ISO 27001 scope, Trust Center permissions, controls mapping spreadsheet, SSO / SAML integration, RBAC model, KMS/HSM key policies, audit log retention and export, VPC/private deployment options, data residency and DPA.

[00:00] Jordan: Alright everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account. Priya is our solutions engineer and Marco from customer success is on the line too.
[00:25] Mark: Thanks, Jordan. We've got Aisha, Liam and Hannah on our side. We've been looking at your docs, wanted to run through SOC 2 / ISO posture and make sure we can map controls back to our audit.
[00:40] Priya: Great — we'll do a high level first then dig into any tech bits you want. Sorry if anything comes out a little robotic, this is a recorded session.
[00:55] Aisha: No problem. Quick ask up front, do you have a recent SOC 2 Type II and an ISO summary? We need the reports for our vendor risk platform.
[01:10] Jordan: Yes, we have the SOC 2 Type II for 2025 and an ISO 27001 attestation summary. I'll share the PDF and a controls mapping sheet which maps Redwood controls to common control frameworks — SOC 2 criteria and ISO sections.
[01:28] Liam: When you say controls mapping, is that a spreadsheet that explicitly maps to our control IDs? We use a custom matrix so mapping helps.
[01:40] Jordan: Yeah exactly — we'll include a sheets export that has rows for each control, evidence artifacts and where to find them in the trust center.
[01:50] Mark: Trust center — we need read-only access for our security team. Is that possible?
[01:58] Priya: Yep, we can grant org-level read-only to external accounts. There's an audit log for accesses to the trust center as well.
[02:10] Aisha: Nice. On encryption — we want to use our KMS, not Redwood-managed keys. How do you support customer-managed keys / HSM?
[02:22] Priya: We support CMEK — customer-managed encryption keys — through KMS integrations. There's a few options depending on deployment: for Hosted API we integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and for Private/VPC we can support HSM backends. I'll send a runbook.
[02:40] Mark: Caveat, our procurement requires keys never be exported and split control between ops and security.
[02:48] Priya: Understood — the key policies we recommend can enforce that. For private deployments we can also support a bring-your-own-HSM model where the HSM is customer-hosted.
[03:02] Hannah: From legal side, we need to confirm DPA coverage for data residency and deletion timelines.
[03:10] Jordan: We'll surface the DPA and any addendum language. We usually include standard EU data residency options and deletion SLA tiers.
[03:18] Marco: Quick note — some of the links in the trust center are descriptively titled so sometimes customers expect one-click for evidence, but we can walk through how to download artifacts.
[03:30] Aisha: Ok let's get into audit logs — what logs are retained, retention windows, and how can we export them to our SIEM?
[03:40] Priya: Audit logs include API access, admin console actions, and trust center events. Retention defaults to 90 days in hosted, with add-ons for longer retention. Exports go to S3 or we can stream to a syslog / SIEM via our pipeline.
[03:55] Liam: Is there an endpoint to pull logs programmatically?
[04:00] Priya: Yes, we have a logs API and S3 export; for Private deployments the logs can stay inside your VPC and be forwarded to your SIEM.
[04:12] Mark: About RBAC — can we enforce least privilege for our different teams? We have devs, ops, and security who need varying levels.
[04:20] Priya: We offer role-based roles — sorry, RBAC — with predefined roles and granular permissions. You can also create custom roles and tie them to SSO groups via SAML/SCIM.
[04:32] Aisha: SCIM provisioning — do you support automatic group sync?
[04:36] Priya: Yes SCIM is supported for provisioning groups and users; SAML for SSO. We'll share an example assertion and a sample attribute mapping.
[04:47] Hannah: Do you support Just-in-Time (JIT) provisioning and session timeouts?
[04:52] Priya: We support JIT and configurable session timeout policies — defaults are industry norm but they can be tightened via org policy.
[05:05] Jordan: Quick question — are there any regulatory constraints we should be aware of on your side for PII or PHI?
[05:12] Mark: We're a P&C insurer, we process PHI in some claims workflows. Need to understand how data is protected in transit and at rest and if there are additional controls for PHI.
[05:22] Priya: We recommend Private deployment for workloads with PHI, but hosted can be used with appropriate contractual coverage and customer-managed keys. We also have optional contract clauses and handling processes.
[05:35] Aisha: Can you outline segmentation — e.g., how customer data is isolated?
[05:40] Priya: Multi-tenant isolation is logical with strong tenancy boundaries, network isolation, per-customer encryption, and per-tenant storage buckets. For stricter needs we have Dedicated pools and Private deployments which provide compute and network separation.
[05:56] Liam: What's the process for evidence requests during our audit? Can we request ad-hoc artifacts?
[06:02] Marco: Yes — we have a request flow in the trust center. For large audits we assign a CSM to coordinate evidence collection.
[06:10] Mark: Timeline: we want to run this through our vendor risk tool by March 10th. Is the SOC 2 report shareable by Feb 20th?
[06:20] Jordan: Yes, Feb 20th is fine — I'll upload to the trust center and send the direct link.
[06:26] Aisha: One more tech point — KV cache and streaming, sorry might be out of scope, but want to ensure logs capture model access events and prompt contents are not stored beyond retention.
[06:40] Priya: Good callout — application-level input/output logs are retained per your retention policy; we recommend anonymization for PII in prompts. Prompt data for hosted inference is encrypted and retention controlled; for Private deployments you can set local retention.
[06:58] Mark: Any mishearings — we had a vendor earlier say K-V cash instead of cache, haha.
[07:04] (laughter)
[07:08] Priya: On data residency — we have region pinning for both compute and storage. For EU-only you can pin to eu-west regions and the trust center shows pinned regions per tenant.
[07:20] Liam: If we do private deployment in our cloud account, what parts remain in Redwood control plane?
[07:27] Priya: For Private there's a control plane that can be customer-managed or Redwood-managed depending on agreement. The control plane handles updates and metrics; for air-gapped we provide an appliance model.
[07:40] Hannah: For legal, need an inventory of subprocessors. Do you have a current list?
[07:45] Jordan: Yes we maintain a subprocessors list in the trust center and will include it in the package.
[07:52] Mark: About ISO 27001 — do you have scope documentation and certification date?
[07:58] Jordan: We have ISO 27001:2013 certification (certificate) through 2024 audit cycle and a scope document. We'll include the certificate image and summary.
[08:10] Aisha: Can you map your ISO controls to our internal control IDs?
[08:14] Jordan: We can include a mapping sheet; it won't be a 1:1 for every internal ID but we'll set the columns so you can map easily.
[08:22] Liam: On RBAC again — can we force MFA for admin roles and separate duties?
[08:28] Priya: Yes MFA is supported org-wide and can be required for specific roles. We also have session-level approval and privileged access workflows.
[08:40] Mark: How do you handle incident response notifications? SLA for incident communication?
[08:46] Marco: Our playbook includes 24-hour initial notification for sev 1 incidents, with a post-mortem and timelines. For enterprise customers we can sync SLAs in contract.
[08:58] Aisha: Related — are audit logs tamper-evident? Hashing or append-only storage?
[09:05] Priya: We use append-only storage with signed hashes for critical admin logs; those artifacts can be exported to customer-controlled buckets for long-term retention.
[09:16] Mark: For forensic requests, do you provide raw disk artifacts if needed?
[09:22] Priya: Typically we provide log exports and snapshots; raw disk artifacts are handled case-by-case through legal and specific protocols.
[09:30] Hannah: Okay, from legal there might be an NDA or 3rd party attestation we need — we'll follow-up.
[09:36] Jordan: Sounds good. Priya, maybe now would be a good time to walk briefly through an example trust center artifact?
[09:44] Priya: Sure — I'll narrate, I'm going to point to the SOC 2 report item, the control mapping sheet, and the subprocessors list. (brief pause) The SOC 2 PDF shows coverage period Jan 2025-Dec 2025, testing procedures for CC1-CC7. Control mapping has columns: control id, description, evidence link, last updated. Some evidence is automated (logs) and some is manual (policies).
[10:20] Aisha: Where do you store evidence — S3? Will that be in our region?
[10:25] Priya: Evidence artifacts are stored encrypted in region; for hosted we'll align storage region to tenant region. For exports to you, we push to your S3 or provide a time-limited link.
[10:37] Mark: Slightly tangential — what's your penetration testing cadence and do you share reports?
[10:44] Jordan: Annual pen test plus third-party scan results; summary findings are shareable and critical remediation evidence is in the trust center. Full pen test reports are limited access and we usually share redacted versions under an NDA.
[10:58] Liam: For our SOC 2 mapping, we need evidence IDs that match your internal system so we can automate pulls. Is that available?
[11:06] Marco: Yes we include unique artifact IDs and an API to pull evidence links. We'll provide API credentials for read-only programmatic access upon agreement.
[11:18] Aisha: A few nitty-gritty questions: do you rotate keys automatically, and what's your KMS key rotation policy?
[11:26] Priya: We can configure automatic rotation; default rotation cadence is 90 days for some keys, customer-managed keys follow the customer's KMS policy.
[11:34] Mark: How about backup encryption and key escrow?
[11:37] Priya: Backups are encrypted with per-tenant keys; key escrow is supported in private deployments if required.
[11:45] Hannah: We might need contract language around breach notification windows — typical window?
[11:50] Jordan: Standard is 72 hours for data breaches that materially affect customer data, but we can negotiate different windows for enterprise contracts.
[11:58] Mark: Ok let's talk about an example mapping for a single control — access control: data access logging and review. How is that demonstrated?
[12:10] Priya: We show logs, periodic access review records, ticketing evidence for access requests, and retention policies. Those are captured as artifacts with timestamps and hashed checksums.
[12:25] Aisha: If we need longer retention for logs (say 1 year), what's the pricing or add-on?
[12:30] Marco: That's an add-on — we can provide a quote once we know volumes.
[12:36] Liam: About private deployment — what's the onboarding timeline? We estimate 8-12 weeks historically.
[12:42] Priya: Typical Private onboarding is 6-10 weeks depending on custom network/workload items; Dedicated pools slightly faster. We'll draft a proposed timeline for your environment.
[12:54] Mark: Any limitations on export of PII from your data lake? For regulatory reasons, we need strict egress controls.
[13:02] Priya: Egress can be restricted via network ACLs and IAM roles. For hosted we provide controls and monitoring, but dedicated/private gives you stronger egress controls.
[13:12] Aisha: One more — can we have alerting for anomalous admin behavior?
[13:16] Priya: Yes we have behavior analytics and admin anomaly detection that can generate alerts to your SIEM or to our ops team depending on severity.
[13:28] Jordan: Alright folks we're getting towards the end of the hour. Quick recap and next steps: I'll share SOC 2 & ISO artifacts, Priya will prepare the KMS/HSM runbook and sample SAML/SCIM config, Marco will prepare a quote for extended log retention and timelines for Private onboarding. Mark/Hannah will share contract and data residency specifics.
[13:52] Mark: That works. For trust center access, Jordan, please send an invite to Aisha and Liam and give them read-only.
[13:58] Jordan: Will do — I'll request external read-only access.
[14:02] Hannah: Legal will send our standard DPA redlines and a list of subprocessors we need to validate.
[14:07] Marco: Noted.
[14:10] (brief crosstalk)
[14:20] Aisha: Thanks — one logistic: are there export controls for logs containing PII? Just want to confirm masking options.
[14:26] Priya: We support data masking and redaction pre-export; we'll document best practices and sample configs.
[14:36] Mark: Good. Anything else?
[14:40] Jordan: If not, we'll follow up with the package by Feb 20th and propose a deep technical session for the KMS integration week of Feb 23rd.
[14:50] Liam: Works for us.
[14:54] Marco: I'll include an item in the CSM plan to coordinate the audit.
[14:58] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll send notes and the access links.
[15:04] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attributions and minor transcription errors present (e.g., kv cache pronounced as K-V cash in recording), filler words and brief crosstalk retained.

References / Links mentioned: Trust Center (will be shared) — https://trust.redwood.ai (placeholder), SOC 2 Type II 2025, ISO 27001 summary, controls mapping spreadsheet, KMS runbook, SAML/SCIM sample.

End of transcript.
